figures.name: Fig1_two_shear_fields
figures.caption: Defined mechanical fields on actual original surface at rest. Arrows: 1000 Pa = 71.4 µm. Counter-rotating planar Gaussian streamfunction is inspired by vortex morphology, not a reproduction of a bubble solution.

figures.name: Fig2_uniform_surface_following
figures.caption: Actual original-ID facets at each accepted state, area/normal updated. Top: full body; bottom: retained-facet detail with actual coordinates, no deformation magnification. Broken-edge unsupported triangles are omitted from loads, not removed from the material graph. Axes fit actual positions per panel.

figures.name: Fig2_counter_rotating_surface_following
figures.caption: Actual original-ID facets at each accepted state, area/normal updated. Top: full body; bottom: retained-facet detail with actual coordinates, no deformation magnification. Broken-edge unsupported triangles are omitted from loads, not removed from the material graph. Axes fit actual positions per panel.

figures.name: Fig3_current_native_force_mapping
figures.caption: Actual native external-force arrays at each mode’s first failure, surface detail with physical coordinates. Positive 1/3 barycentric map uses current triangles; no signed affine V3 weights. Facet arrows follow Figure 2 scale; native force arrows 1 µN = 50 µm.

figures.name: Fig4_crack_network_evolution
figures.caption: Current coordinates of actual damaged original bonds, anchors retained. A colored endpoint is not an inferred wetted crack face. Final bridges cross the historical diagnostic upper volume; no bonds are deleted by analysis.

figures.name: Fig4b_failed_networks_vs_true_fragments
figures.caption: Independent graphs: failed bonds define damage clusters; surviving bonds define real material components. Initial cuts and contact do not count as natural fractures or cohesion.

figures.name: Fig5_true_detached_fragments
figures.caption: Full actual final extents. Original surviving material bonds and anchor reachability alone identify components; contact/proximity never merges fragments. Colors may repeat.

figures.name: Fig6_fragment_size_distribution
figures.caption: Zero bins remain zero. Equal original material volumes determine mass; anchors excluded. Requested bins cross the 20-node target threshold; exact 20–200 is reported separately.

figures.name: Fig7_actual_energy_ledger
figures.caption: Work uses current force along actual native drift. Passive drag is physical-proxy dissipation, separate from irreversible material damage. Numerical residual and contact activation remain explicit; no fitted energy correction.

figures.name: Fig8_final_controlled_comparison
figures.caption: A versus B isolates the spatial mode within the new follower protocol. It does not isolate follower geometry relative to older dead-load experiments; actual slip peaks and work are not matched.

figures.name: Fig9_surface_coverage_and_force
figures.caption: Retained original exterior faces only. Loss of all represented faces on a fragment means unresolved hydrodynamics, not a claim that its real fluid force is zero. New crack wetting remains unresolved.
